summary: Arthur Maurice Hocart (1883–1939) was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist educated at Elizabeth College and Exeter College. He served as Ceylon's Archaeological Commissioner (1921–1929), Honorary Lecturer at UCL (1931–1934), and Professor of Sociology at Cairo University (1934).

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin under Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf, and Jena (PhD ~1813). He also attended lectures by Friedrich Majer (~1813–1814) and held a Dozentur at Berlin in 1820.

Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist educated at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. Joining the Indian Education Service in 1881, he was Professor and Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1881 and 1914, and Professor at Allahabad (1914–1918).

Arthur Waley (1889–1966) worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at King's College, Cambridge, he studied with Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi, and served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

Arthur Wilhelm Gleye (1867–1937) was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Tartu (~1888–1893) under Leo Meyer. From 1901 to 1921, he served as Lecturer of German at Tomsk State University.

Indologist Arthur William Ryder (1877–1938) studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman at Harvard and Ernst Windisch at Leipzig (PhD 1901). He held teaching posts at Harvard (1901–1906) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall (1851–1912) was an academic educated at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand (born 1966) works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at McGill University and the University of Calgary, and became an Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto (~2002).

Artur Kibat (1878–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Adalbert Bezzenberger and earned his PhD at the University of Königsberg (1898–1904). In 1910, he was a teacher at Oberrealschule Wilhelmshaven.
Aruna Haldar (born 1918) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and later served as a teacher at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani (1921–2003) was an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Mumbai (~1947–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma (born 1940) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard, he taught at Queensland and Sydney before being appointed Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill University in 1994.

Aryadeva (200–250) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was associated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning and taught numerous disciples, including Candrakīrti and Shakyamitra.
Aryendra Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Walther Wüst by 1939. He served as Director at Osmania University (attested 1969).

Asanga Tilakaratne (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Peradeniya and Hawaiʻi (PhD), he held professorships at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Kelaniya (~2003–2009), later becoming Emeritus Professor at Colombo (~2017).
Asatoshi Kamiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Aschwin Lippe (1914–1988) worked in Indology, Sinology, and archaeology, receiving a PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin (~1934–1942). He served as a curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1949–1973) and the University of Paris (1980).

Asen Balikci (1929–2019) was an anthropologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD at Columbia University in 1956. He held posts at the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968) and taught at the Université de Montréal from 1963 to 1993.

Ashok Aklujkar (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy educated at Pune and Harvard (PhD ~1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).
